title: Adaptive audit fidelity PRD — ML sampler + fastpath playbook
content:
Context
-----
Problem: customers with regulated, customer-managed VPCs want strong auditability for network/approval events but cannot retain full fidelity logs indefinitely (cost + privacy). Current PRDs in this folder focus on approval gates and compact evidence formats; this draft proposes an "adaptive audit fidelity" approach that dynamically varies audit sampling and evidence fidelity based on risk signals, plus a fast approval/rollback runbook for emergency operator flows.

Why this matters
- Reduce storage and query costs for long-tail customers while preserving forensic value for high-risk changes
- Enable conservative defaults for enterprise SLAs and a lower-cost mode for SMBs
- Provide repeatable operator playbook for emergency changes that still produce verifiable artifacts

Goals
- Define an ML-backed sampling service (Sampler) that:
  * ingests event stream (change requests, approvals, operator annotations, traffic anomalies)
  * scores events for audit-fidelity (0..1) and decides full vs compact evidence retention
  * exposes policy controls (customer knob + Redwood tier overrides)
- Design a compact-but-verifiable evidence envelope for sampled-off events (hash commitments + minimal metadata)
- Define approval gate behaviors and an emergency fastpath with attestation receipts
- Instrument metrics and retention SLAs to measure forensic coverage and cost impact

Non-goals
- Replacing customer SIEMs or proposing a full forensic query engine.
- Changing the canonical approval UX (we keep current UX, add policy hooks).

High-level approach
1) Sampler service (stateless controller + model):
   - Accepts event proto: {change_id, actor, change_type, diff_summary, route, time, pre-change telemetry keys} (we'll map to existing event schema).
   - Model features: change surface area (ports, rules modified), presence/absence of delegated admin, recent failure rate for tenant, change window, operator trust tier, anomaly signals from telemetry (spike in connections), customer-supplied risk tags.
   - Output: fidelity_score + reason_codes (explainable short tokens).
   - Decision: if fidelity_score > threshold -> store full evidence blob; else -> store compact envelope (signed hash, minimal metadata, pointer to ephemeral snapshot if available).

2) Evidence envelope design (compact):
   - fields (compact): change_id, timestamp, actor, decision, short diff summary (<=2 lines), hash_commitment, signature_by_service, retention_tier_tag, provenance_tags.
   - hash_commitment is SHA256 over canonicalized diff blob; full blob optionally archived for X days (customer-configurable).
   - store compact records in long-term cheap store; full blobs live in higher-cost tier.

3) Emergency fastpath + operator runbook:
   - Use case: customer operator needs to unblock production (eg misconfigured egress) and approvals would cause unacceptable outage.
   - Fastpath flow: operator issues emergency-change (flagged), provide short justification; system allows immediate apply but automatically upsamples audit fidelity for last N related events and attaches a time-limited immutable evidence snapshot.
   - Post-event: mandatory postmortem submission (owner required within 24h) that includes operator rationale and linked artifacts. Failure to submit triggers auto-escalation.
   - For legal/forensics, fastpath attaches cryptographic receipt (service signature + monotonic counter + change diff hash) tied to customer key (where available).

4) Customer-configurable policy knobs:
   - baseline_mode: conservative | balanced | lean
   - dedicated_thresholds: a mapping of event types -> fidelity threshold (override defaults)
   - emergency_policy: allowed_roles, TTL, required_postmortem_window
   - SLO settings for retention cost caps (monthly budget alerting)

Observability & metrics
- forensic_coverage_pct: percent of high-risk changes retained full-fidelity
- sampling_precision/recall proxies (via synthetic-eval corpus in CI)
- avg_storage_cost_per_tenant_slot
- fastpath_count by customer and by reason_code
- time_to_postmortem_submission

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (experiment): offline sampler evaluation run against historical event corpus. (Data team -> create evaluation harness, JIRA-PI-1123)
- Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in pilot with 3 customers -> Sampler in decision-only mode (no storage changes), produce alerts + suggested retention. Collect feedback.
- Phase 2 (soft-launch): pilot customers enabled to switch baseline_mode; we introduce compact envelopes and archival TTLs for sampled events.
- Phase 3 (GA): expose policy controls in Console, billing meter for retention tiers, and SLOs.

Operator UX & console hooks (high level)
- UI: per-customer Audit policy page with slider for baseline_mode, per-change-type thresholds, and emergency-role list.
- Timeline view: show chain of evidence for a change (compact vs full) and quick links to request full blob retrieval for N days (cost estimate shown).

Security & cryptography notes
- Service signs commitments with rotating service key; customer-managed KMS integration provides optional customer-signed receipts.
- Store minimal metadata in low-privilege DB; full blobs in encrypted blob store with per-customer encryption keys (rotate per policy).
- We should draft an internal threat model (follow-up) and ensure legal/infosec review.

Open questions / risks
- Q: What is the acceptable false-negative rate for not keeping full evidence for an event that later needs it?
- Q: How to bootstrap training data for ML sampler without overfitting to current tenants? (proposal: synthetic corpora + red-team-created incidents)
- Q: Can compact envelopes be forensically sufficient for regulators in all jurisdictions? (likely not; need jurisdictional override)
- Risk: customer legal teams may demand full retention; product must surface an easy SLA upgrade path.

Implementation tasks (initial backlog)
- [ ] Event schema mapping and ingestion pipeline (eng-infra)
- [ ] Sampler ML model prototype + offline eval harness (applied-ml)
- [ ] Compact envelope schema + signing service (serving-runtime + security)
- [ ] Emergency fastpath API + operator runbook draft (product + sRE)
- [ ] Console policy controls mockups (console team)
- [ ] Billing meter for retained-full-bytes (finance integration)

Acceptance criteria (pilot)
- Sampler produces fidelity decisions with >80% precision on synthetic high-risk set
- Pilot customers can preview suggested retention and opt-in toggles in Console
- Fastpath flow produces signed receipts and enforces postmortem requirement
- Storage cost delta measured and < 20% of projected naive full-retention cost for pilot tenants

Notes / links / scratch items
- Quick eval ideas: take last 6 months of customer change stream, mark postmortem-labeled incidents as positives, train simple tree-based sampler as baseline.
- Slack thread: #prod-oncall (link: slack-redwood://channel/prod-oncall)
- Confluence spec: CONFLUENCE-4567 (design notes + threat model TODO)
- JIRA epic: JIRA-PI-1123

Unresolved TODOs (owner assignments)
- Maya: coordinate offline evaluation dataset by 2025-01-20
- Priya: draft compact-envelope proto + signed-commitment API by 2025-02-05
- Ethan: sketch emergency fastpath API surface and CLI ergonomics by 2025-01-25
- Diego: cost-model for storage tiers (early estimate) by 2025-01-30

Appendix: example scenario
- Scenario: customer deploys a new egress rule that accidentally allows broad internet access. Telemetry shows spike in outbound connections within 2 minutes. Sampler sees: change_type=egress-update, scope=0.0.0.0/0, tenant_anomaly=high -> fidelity_score=0.92 -> keep full blob. If operator used emergency fastpath earlier, system upsamples last 10 related events and attaches receipts for future forensics.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally exploratory. Looking for feedback on:
- feasibility of ML sampling in an auditable way
- legal constraints we should surface early
- integration complexity with existing approval gate flows
__notes: Working doc: informal sections, TODOs, and open questions present. Not final; will be iterated with applied-ml and security.
